adultGuide.title: Bookend Story Evidence Adult Guide: ____________________.
setupSteps: Set out one evidence card, six blank paper strips, and a pencil before the adult-led session begins: ____________________.
Label the strips story claim, first clue, second clue, because line, evidence sentence, and bookend note: ____________________.
Choose one pretend story world and keep every character, place, object, clue, and reason invented: ____________________.
Tell the writer that dictated words, adult-scribed words, or independent writing all fit the offline paper-only activity: ____________________.
Place the story claim strip at the left edge and the bookend note at the right edge so the invented evidence has a calm start and close: ____________________.
facilitationNotes: Start with a small story claim, not a big explanation: ____________________.
Ask for the first clue as one pretend detail the writer can point to on paper: ____________________.
Ask for the second clue as another invented detail that helps the same story claim: ____________________.
Use the because line to connect the two clues before asking for the evidence sentence: ____________________.
Close with the bookend note so the writer can name what the evidence helped show in the fictional story: ____________________.
safetyNotes: Use invented characters, broad pretend places, and made-up clue details only: ____________________.
Keep the activity offline, paper-only, adult-led, and away from outside audiences: ____________________.
Skip any prompt that starts to ask for real names, real place details, or personal facts: ____________________.
Keep the evidence sentence about the pretend story, not about a real person or real event: ____________________.
Treat the bookend note as a private paper close for this session: ____________________.

evidenceRoutines.title: Story Claim Bookend: ____________________.
evidenceRoutines.useWhen: Use when the writer needs one simple idea to hold the evidence path: ____________________.
steps: The adult places the story claim strip at the left edge of the workspace: ____________________.
The adult asks what small idea could be true inside the pretend story: ____________________.
The writer completes this line: My story claim is ____________________.
The adult rereads the story claim and saves it for the evidence sentence: ____________________.

evidenceRoutines.title: First Clue Finder: ____________________.
evidenceRoutines.useWhen: Use when the story claim needs one invented detail to begin the evidence path: ____________________.
steps: The adult points to the first clue strip and asks what pretend detail helps the story claim: ____________________.
The writer chooses one object, action, sound, color, sign, or tiny change from the fictional world: ____________________.
The writer completes this line: My first clue is ____________________.
The adult places the first clue beside the story claim without adding real details: ____________________.

evidenceRoutines.title: Second Clue Pair: ____________________.
evidenceRoutines.useWhen: Use when the writer has one clue and needs another clue that supports the same story claim: ____________________.
steps: The adult rereads the story claim and first clue in order: ____________________.
The writer names a different invented detail that points toward the same idea: ____________________.
The writer completes this line: My second clue is ____________________.
The adult checks that the second clue helps the same story claim instead of starting a new idea: ____________________.

evidenceRoutines.title: Because Line Link: ____________________.
evidenceRoutines.useWhen: Use when the clues are ready but the connection is still missing: ____________________.
steps: The adult lays the first clue and second clue strips between the story claim and the blank because line: ____________________.
The adult asks why both clues help the story claim in the pretend story: ____________________.
The writer completes this line: These clues help because ____________________.
The adult trims the because line to one clear reason and keeps it fictional: ____________________.

evidenceRoutines.title: Evidence Sentence Builder: ____________________.
evidenceRoutines.useWhen: Use when the writer is ready to combine the story claim, two clues, and because line: ____________________.
steps: The adult reads the story claim, first clue, second clue, and because line in order: ____________________.
The writer points to the strip that should start the evidence sentence: ____________________.
The writer completes this line: My evidence sentence is ____________________.
The adult helps keep the evidence sentence to one clear fictional story sentence: ____________________.

evidenceRoutines.title: Bookend Note Close: ____________________.
evidenceRoutines.useWhen: Use at the end of a paper session to close the evidence path neatly: ____________________.
steps: The adult places the bookend note strip at the right edge of the workspace: ____________________.
The adult rereads the evidence sentence without adding new facts: ____________________.
The writer completes this line: My bookend note says ____________________.
The adult stacks the strips in order for a private paper folder: ____________________.

takeHomeEvidenceSlips.title: Story Claim Slip
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.adultNote: Ask for one small idea that could be true inside the pretend story.

takeHomeEvidenceSlips.title: First Clue Slip
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.adultNote: Choose one invented detail that helps the story claim.

takeHomeEvidenceSlips.title: Second Clue Slip
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.adultNote: Choose a different pretend detail that helps the same story claim.

takeHomeEvidenceSlips.title: Because Line Slip
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.adultNote: Use one plain reason that stays inside the fictional story.

takeHomeEvidenceSlips.title: Evidence Sentence Slip
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.adultNote: Combine the story claim, first clue, second clue, and because line in one sentence.

takeHomeEvidenceSlips.title: Bookend Note Slip
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.adultNote: Close with one short note about what the evidence helped show.

takeHomeEvidenceSlips.title: Clue Match Slip
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.prompt: The first clue and second clue both help the story claim because ____________________.
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.adultNote: Reread both clue strips before filling the blank.

takeHomeEvidenceSlips.title: Claim Check Slip
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.prompt: The story claim still fits after I read the clues: ____________________.
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.adultNote: Use this as a quiet paper check, not a correction mark.

takeHomeEvidenceSlips.title: Sentence Shorten Slip
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.prompt: One extra detail I can leave off the evidence sentence is ____________________.
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.adultNote: Frame this as paper sorting so the sentence stays clear.

takeHomeEvidenceSlips.title: Bookend Path Slip
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.prompt: My paper path goes story claim, first clue, second clue, because line, evidence sentence, bookend note: ____________________.
takeHomeEvidenceSlips.adultNote: Close by stacking the strips in order for another adult-led session.

optionalAdultPrompts: Which story claim feels small enough for one paper strip: ____________________.
What first clue can the writer invent without using real people or real places: ____________________.
What second clue helps the same story claim in a different way: ____________________.
Which clue should the adult reread before the because line: ____________________.
How can the because line use plain words and stay inside the pretend story: ____________________.
What evidence sentence uses the story claim, first clue, second clue, and because line: ____________________.
What bookend note gives the evidence path a calm paper close: ____________________.
Which strip can stay blank until the writer is ready to dictate or write it: ____________________.
